summary: Maryland rear range light in Chesapeake Bay, built 1873-75 on nine granite piers under a cast-iron frame; Coast Guard-owned, reached by boat, not open to the public.

lens.where: lantern room; described in 2002 as a classic Fresnel lens in poor condition, brass frame marked HENRY - LEPAUTE a PARIS

structures.material: wood tower inside cast-iron corner columns, on nine granite piers
structures.note: Built 1873-75 (temporary light 20 Nov 1873; completed March 1875); alterations 1884, 1888, 1897 (nomination)

staffing.note: Keeper's house removed shortly after automation in 1937 (nomination)

access.note: Coast Guard aid to navigation, reached by boat (nomination); USLHS: not open to the public

events.note: Temporary light shown from the unfinished structure on 20 November 1873
Frame and piers completed March 1875 after the second appropriation of $45,000 (23 June 1874)
Extensive repairs in June 1884: decayed wooden braces replaced by iron swivel and Phoenix beam braces
Cyclone of 21 August 1888 removed the dwelling roof, copper smokestack and part of the tower sheathing
Decayed base timbers replaced and strengthened with iron rods and beams
Fiscal year ended 30 June 1899: new model fourth-order lamps installed; minor repairs (Board report)
Keeper Harry H. Wills and assistant Robert Williams sheltered two men from a disabled gasoline launch on 17 May; next day one injured man was helped to medical treatment
Electrified in April 1929: submarine cable to land lines, 94-watt railway headlight lamp, astronomic clock; candlepower 20,000 to 140,000; about $1,050
Automated 1937; keeper's house removed shortly after (nomination)
Coast Guard engineering survey (20 April 1994) calls the wooden tower a serious safety hazard and proposes demolition and a light-lowering device
Coast Guard repairs: single-pane Plexiglas with vents in window openings; watch-room banister replaced; spare range light removed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1873 first-light date in the record (Rowlett, Wikidata) matches the temporary light the nomination dates to 20 November 1873; construction ran to March 1875.

corrections.why: The NRHP nomination documents construction in 1873-75 and alterations in 1884, 1888 and 1897 and does not mention an 1886 tower. The USLHS place record gives 'Year Tower Established: 1886' with no explanation. Needs a human check against the Board's 1886 report before any change.
The USLHS place record marks active_aton false, while the station record says active. No source read settles the current status; the story does not state it.

notes_for_editor: Construction, repair and cyclone details rest on the 2002 NRHP nomination, which quotes Lighthouse Board reports for 1870-1899. Those Board reports for the 1870s-1880s are not in the local corpus, so they are cited only through the nomination. The USLHS and Rowlett/Wikidata 1886 'present tower' is not supported by the nomination (see corrections). Keeper first name: the 1914 Bulletin text reads 'Harry H. Wills' (OCR, clear in running text) while the 1912-1917 index and the USLHS roster read 'Henry H. Wills'; unresolved. Keeper dates are the archive's roster, matched by name and position, and were not checked against NARA registers. Bernhard Berends is linked to the lower range front by the archive's own person record only (other_stations); not confirmed in a primary record. The 1899 Board volume is the report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1899, so the lamps date to July 1898 to June 1899. Bulletin 1924 p. 6 says the rear light changed 'fixed to occulting, oil to electric incandescent'; the 1924-1929 index says 'changed to flashing'; these conflict and none is dated to a specific event, so the record's characteristic (F W, ENC) was not changed and no characteristic is printed in the story. Bulletin 1912-1917 index p. 275 lists 'Craighill Channel Range Rear Auxiliary, light established' and Commissioner 1917 lists 'Craighill Channel Range Rear Lower'; neither was located in the text and neither is used. The record's tower height (32.0 m, OSM) was not confirmed by any source read; the nomination gives none, so the story gives no height. Chronicling America searches for this station returned unrelated pages; no newspaper is used. The official website (craighillrange.org) returned HTTP 403 and was not read. The USLHS place record marks active_aton false; the station record says active. The story does not state the current status. NEWSPAPERS (resume run): a Chronicling America search for 'Craighill Channel' with 'light keeper' in Maryland papers, 1886-1917, returned four pages; the one page read (Evening Capital, Annapolis, 12 March 1892) mentions a 'Craighill Channel light at Fair Haven', which is not this station, so it is not used; the other three hits were not read. No newspaper is used in the story. FACT-CHECK 2026-10-22: the 1899 Board entry ('604. Craighill Channel (rear)') and the 1914 Bulletin rescue text were read from OCR running text; the page images were not viewed. The 1912-1917 index entry reads 'Wills, Henry H., keeper Craighill Channel Range, rescue 124': it does not say 'rear', so the link to this station is by keeper name and the 1914 rescue. A 1924 Bulletin line also reads 'Harry H. Wills, keeper, Fifth district, retired' in a column-split OCR block; it is not used because the page image has not been checked.
